checklist.notes: One-event lines, sequence markers, and capitalized focus words make expected structure and stress choices explicit.
Four short events and one collocation/stress pattern fit the 35-minute foundation lesson.
Sequence, decision language, and information focus are carried into the learner’s final written and spoken story.
A four-event account, make/made a decision, and contrastive sentence stress directly address sequencing, lexical combination, and information focus.
The lesson moves from reading and ordering to collocation noticing, contrastive stress, and creation of a parallel account.
The numbered model, collocation contrast, stress models, recording, event recovery, and final retell provide sufficient explanation and bounded feedback.
Visible prominence cues and replay checks offer accessible pronunciation support without unsupported group claims.

findings.description: The ordering check leaves First/Next/Then/Finally in the lines and does not ask the learner to shuffle them, so numbering 1–4 mostly copies overt sequence cues rather than testing event-order comprehension.
findings.recommendation: Present the four lines in a deliberately mixed order or temporarily hide the sequence markers before asking the learner to reconstruct the order.
